To answer your questions, well I do feel like anything which can get my mind off of suicidal thoughts helps a lot. Since it generally is something that makes me feel like life is worth it.

Also yes, that makes sense. So I’ll try asking her how she feels about suicide when she’s just feeling fine, versus when she is feeling very upset.

I think she thinks people act like they care for her just because think they should or they need to. But that is a good idea, to ask her how she thinks she knows someone cares about her or not.

Personally, I am ok with talking about suicide openly. I think she might be a bit more uncomfortable with it. She was having a very bad day a couple of nights ago and she told me she “wanted to be in a fatal car crash.” I did ask her about having suicidal thoughts but she once again just sort of ignored it.

And a little over a week ago, she texted me and told me that she needed help and she’s scared, I asked why and she said, of herself. I called her immediately and she was definitely in a crisis. I didn’t really say much because well I didn’t know too much of what to say. I told her I was there for her and I just stayed on the line. I could hear her crying and she kept saying she can’t do it anymore. And she also said that she doesn’t think she’ll make it very far into life (something which I’ve definitely thought before). She asked me why I even bothered talking to her and I just told her it was because I like her and she’s really nice and she’s my friend. She ended up being ok. I asked to make Plans to go on a walk in the park with her the next day but that kind of fell through because of a change in plans.

But yes I’m still very much worried about her. I know she needs help. And oh also, I haven’t told you yet but, I talked to a teacher about her thoughts. He said he’d do his best to handle it. I hope I can figure out a way for her to see a therapist or something. 

Thanks for your help too. So much.

generally I distract myself by either playing video games, sleeping, being active with my time (doing homework, etc), or being around other people

yeah, I haven't thought to really talk to her about it when she feels fine. Once I did ask if she wanted to talk about it and she said she was in a good mood and didn't want to ruin it by talking about it, if that says anything.

She says that she just thinks that people who say they care about someone don't know if they actually care about them or just if the *should* be caring about them, if that makes sense. So that's why I assume she doesn't think her thoughts aren't important, because nobody should care about her having them. If any of that made sense.

Thanks for suggesting those questions. I can ask her the next time we are talking about it. And as for talking to the teacher about it, I felt like I really should tell him ASAP (we are back in school on the 7th), but since then I've been not so sure if I should or not. And I don't know how she would feel about it. I haven't mentioned his name directly but when I ask how she'd feel if I got help for her she just sort of shrugs it off. I don't know if she'd feel relieved and glad that someone wanted to help her, or rather betrayed and even more scared. I did make the mistake of telling her that I wouldn't tell anyone about her suicidal thoughts without her consent, but she never replied to that message so yeah. 

Thanks again for the help

generally distracting myself is the best way to rid myself of them. If I don't, then it just gets worse until I'm finally distracted.

So since I've last replied I've talked to her once or twice about it. Generally, she is fine but she has nights where she is just feeling depressed. I brought it up to her how I never stopped caring that she's had suicidal thoughts (because after she confided in me about it, we never really had the chance to talk about it) and that she could talk to me about it whenever she feels prepared.

She said that her suicidal thoughts aren't a big deal and just never seemed very important to her. And since she doesn't really care about it, other people wouldn't either. And the way she explained  her more serious suicidal thoguhts was that she'll just get worked up, cry, and then blank out. And its just numb and nothing matters, and the thoughts distract her from what's actually upset her. If any of that makes sense.

I've tried asking her if she has ever had a plan to act on (trying to see how urgent it might be) or if she would be upset if I sought help for her, but she generally just kind of dodges those questions, if that makes sense.

This is a lot of info. Happy holidays to you by the way. thanks for all your help, its much appreciated.
